questions.q: What three things should Support's page let a Support lead answer at a glance, per this lesson?
options: Whether ticket volume is trending up or down, which categories are driving it, and what's open right now
The subscriber's billing history, payment method, and credit score
The exact SQL used to build the underlying Snowflake views
The warehouse size and current credit consumption
questions.explain: These three questions come directly from Support's original ask in Lesson 1, restated as what the page needs to make answerable at a glance.

questions.q: Why is Power BI's automatic 'Sum of ticket_count' correct for this page's visuals, with no custom DAX measure needed?
options: vw_support_ticket_trends already pre-aggregated with COUNT(*) in SQL, so summing those rows back up is correct, not double-counting
Power BI cannot create custom DAX measures against Snowflake data sources
ticket_count is a text column, so no aggregation applies
DAX measures are only valid in DirectQuery mode, and this project uses Import
questions.explain: Since the view already aggregated ticket_count by week/category/priority in SQL, Power BI's default Sum correctly re-aggregates that pre-summed column.

questions.q: Which view feeds the open-tickets table visual on Support's page?
options: vw_support_open_tickets
vw_finance_refunds
vw_support_ticket_trends
raw.tickets_api_raw
questions.explain: vw_support_open_tickets filters to tickets not yet resolved or closed, feeding the table visual directly.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the category and priority slicers on this page?
options: To give Support a real self-service page they can filter and slice themselves, without asking anyone to re-run a query
To restrict which Snowflake role can view the page
To control how often Power BI refreshes the underlying data
To hide the open-tickets table until a filter is applied
questions.explain: The slicers are the real self-service drill-down pattern Support originally asked for in Lesson 1.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an unnecessary DAX measure here would be a bad idea, not just unneeded?
options: It would be one more place a mistake could hide, for no real benefit over the already-correct auto-aggregation
DAX measures always run slower than auto-aggregation in every case
Snowflake views are incompatible with any DAX measure by design
Power BI limits each report to a fixed number of DAX measures
questions.explain: Since the view's pre-aggregated column already sums correctly, adding a custom measure would add complexity without adding correctness.
